title: Settings every solver will take

blocks.text: An airline's crew-pairing service runs on whichever solver its configuration names, and its operators set four things: a time budget in seconds, a relative gap, a thread count and a random seed. They can also ask a MILP solve to stop at its first plan, for a quick feasibility check. The service must never send a parameter the chosen solver refuses, because in OR-Tools 9.15 a refusal stops the solve.
Write `params_for(solver, seconds, rel_gap, threads, seed, first_plan=False)` in `params.py`. It returns a `mathopt.SolveParameters` with:

items: `time_limit` set to `seconds` as a `datetime.timedelta`, and `relative_gap_tolerance` set to `rel_gap`, for every solver;
`threads` set to `threads`, except for HiGHS, which refuses the common parameter;
`random_seed` set to `seed`, except for PDLP, which refuses it;
`solution_limit=1` when `first_plan` is true, for HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT only (GLOP and PDLP solve LPs and refuse a solution limit).

blocks.text: Every field you do not set stays at its default, `None`, which means the solver's own default. The tests build the parameters for each solver and solve a model with them, so a refused setting shows up as an exception from `mathopt.solve`.

cases.says: every solver gets the time limit as a timedelta and the relative gap
SCIP and CP-SAT get the thread count and the seed, and solve with them
HiGHS gets no thread count, still gets the seed, and solves with them
PDLP gets no seed, still gets the thread count, and solves with them
asking for the first plan sets solution_limit=1 on HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT and nothing on GLOP or PDLP, and every solver runs
